fig_baseline_ladder_overview: Overview of the progressive baseline ladder architecture. Starting from a SegFormer-B2 encoder with SharedFPN, auxiliary morphological heads are incrementally added: B0 (mask-only), B1a (+clDice loss), B2 (+skeleton distance transform head), B3 (+endpoint/junction heads), and B5 (+width head). Below, three post-hoc graph extraction methods operate on predicted masks and DT maps to produce crack graphs.
fig_multiseed_baseline_comparison: Multi-seed comparison of baseline methods on mIoU_fg (3 seeds: 42, 123, 7). Error bars show standard deviation; black dots show individual seed values. Neither B1a (clDice, p=0.822) nor B2_best (skeleton DT, p=0.145) achieves statistically significant improvement over the B0 mask-only baseline. The dashed line indicates the B0 mean for reference.
fig_single_vs_multiseed_overturned: Three cases where single-seed conclusions were overturned by multi-seed validation. (a) B2 skeleton DT appeared to improve mIoU by +1.0% on seed 42, but multi-seed reveals +0.5% +/- 0.3% (p=0.145, not significant). (b) B1a clDice appeared to harm mIoU by -1.6%, but multi-seed shows +0.2% +/- 0.9% (p=0.822, not significant). (c) MixStyle appeared to improve OOD performance by +52%, but multi-seed shows approximately +1% (p=0.878, not significant).
fig_graph_extraction_edge_f1: Post-hoc graph extraction quality measured by edge F1 at three tolerance tiers for the B2_best model. Method A (skeleton extraction) consistently outperforms DT-based methods B (ridge detection) and C (peak detection). Even at the most lenient tolerance (15 px), edge F1 remains below 0.28, indicating fundamental limitations of post-hoc graph extraction from predicted masks.
fig_dg_multiseed_domain_gap: Domain generalization results across 3 seeds for four methods on in-domain (DamSegment) and out-of-domain (s2ds) evaluation. All methods achieve similar in-domain performance (~0.67 mIoU_fg) and similar OOD performance (~0.12 mIoU_fg), with a stable domain gap of approximately 55%. No DG method significantly reduces this gap (p=0.878 for MixStyle vs ERM). Dashed lines indicate ERM baseline means.
fig_p3_overfit_vs_full: Comparison of direct graph prediction (P3) performance between overfit setting (16 training images, 200 epochs) and full training (1275 images, 100 epochs). Dotted lines show go/no-go gate thresholds. All gates pass convincingly in the overfit setting, confirming architectural soundness. However, full training fails on node F1 and edge F1 gates, revealing the auto-label quality ceiling: the model cannot generalize when trained on noisy auto-generated graph labels.
